nodes.summary: For every prime $p$ and every $q \in \mathbb{Q}$, the absolute value attached to the finite place of $\mathbb{Q}$ at $p$, evaluated at $q$, equals the $p$-adic absolute value $|q|_p$ of $q$. Here $|0|_p = 0$, and $|q|_p = p^{-v_p(q)}$ for $q \neq 0$, where $v_p(q)$ is the $p$-adic valuation of $q$.
nodes.title: Absolute value at a finite rational place

nodes.summary: For every $q \in \mathbb{Q}$, the absolute value attached to the infinite place of $\mathbb{Q}$, evaluated at $q$, equals the ordinary absolute value $|q|$ of $q$ viewed as a real number.
nodes.title: Absolute value at the infinite rational place

nodes.summary: For a place $v$ of $\mathbb{Q}$, the absolute value $|\cdot|_v : \mathbb{Q} \to \mathbb{R}$ sends $q \in \mathbb{Q}$ to the ordinary absolute value $|q|$ when $v$ is the infinite place. When $v$ is the finite place at a prime $p$, it sends $q$ to the normalised $p$-adic absolute value $|q|_p$, where $|0|_p = 0$ and $|q|_p = p^{-v_p(q)}$ for $q \neq 0$, with $v_p(q)$ the $p$-adic valuation of $q$.
nodes.title: Absolute value at a rational place

nodes.summary: To each place $v$ of $\mathbb{Q}$ this assigns a complete normed field: the real numbers $\mathbb{R}$ with the usual absolute value when $v$ is the infinite place, and, when $v$ is the finite place at a prime $p$, the field $\mathbb{Q}_p$ of $p$-adic numbers with the $p$-adic norm.
nodes.title: Bundled completed field at a rational place

nodes.summary: A complete normed field bundled with its structure: a type $K$ together with a normed field structure on $K$ for which $K$ is complete with respect to the metric induced by the norm. It is used to package the completed fields $\mathbb{Q}_v$ of $\mathbb{Q}$ at its places $v$.
nodes.title: Bundled complete normed field

nodes.summary: For a place $v$ of $\mathbb{Q}$, the completed field $\mathbb{Q}_v$ is the field $\mathbb{R}$ of real numbers when $v$ is the infinite place and, when $v$ is the finite place at a prime $p$, the field $\mathbb{Q}_p$ of $p$-adic numbers.
nodes.title: Completed field at a rational place

nodes.summary: For every place $v$ of $\mathbb{Q}$, with completed field $\mathbb{Q}_v$, the image of $\mathbb{Q}$ under the canonical embedding $\mathbb{Q} \to \mathbb{Q}_v$ is dense in $\mathbb{Q}_v$.
nodes.title: The rationals are dense in each completion

nodes.summary: Let $v$ be a place of $\mathbb{Q}$, let $|\cdot|_v$ be the absolute value attached to $v$, let $\mathbb{Q}_v$ be the completed field at $v$, and write $(\mathbb{Q}, |\cdot|_v)$ for the field $\mathbb{Q}$ equipped with $|\cdot|_v$. The image of the canonical ring homomorphism $(\mathbb{Q}, |\cdot|_v) \to \mathbb{Q}_v$, which sends each rational number to itself, is dense in $\mathbb{Q}_v$.
nodes.title: Density of the rationals with a place's absolute value in the completion

nodes.summary: For every place $v$ of $\mathbb{Q}$ and every $q \in \mathbb{Q}$, the norm in the completed field $\mathbb{Q}_v$ of the image of $q$ under the canonical embedding $\mathbb{Q} \to \mathbb{Q}_v$ equals $|q|_v$, the absolute value attached to $v$ evaluated at $q$.
nodes.title: Norm of a rational in a completion

nodes.summary: For a place $v$ of $\mathbb{Q}$ with completed field $\mathbb{Q}_v$, the canonical ring homomorphism $\mathbb{Q} \to \mathbb{Q}_v$ sends each rational number to itself, viewed as a real number when $v$ is the infinite place and as a $p$-adic number when $v$ is the finite place at a prime $p$.
nodes.title: Embedding of the rationals into a completion

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a real-valued absolute value on $\mathbb{Q}$ that is nontrivial, that is, $f(x) \ne 1$ for some $x \ne 0$. Then there is a place $v$ of $\mathbb{Q}$ such that $f$ is equivalent to the absolute value $|\cdot|_v$ attached to $v$ (the ordinary absolute value at the infinite place, the $p$-adic absolute value at the prime $p$).
nodes.title: Every nontrivial absolute value on $\mathbb{Q}$ is equivalent to that of a place

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a real-valued absolute value on $\mathbb{Q}$ that is nontrivial, that is, $f(x) \ne 1$ for some $x \ne 0$. Then there is exactly one place $v$ of $\mathbb{Q}$ such that $f$ is equivalent to the absolute value $|\cdot|_v$ attached to $v$ (the ordinary absolute value at the infinite place, the $p$-adic absolute value at the prime $p$).
nodes.title: Ostrowski's theorem for $\mathbb{Q}$, indexed by places

nodes.summary: The set $M_{\mathbb{Q}}$ of places of $\mathbb{Q}$, which indexes the inequivalent normalised absolute values on $\mathbb{Q}$. It consists of one infinite place, corresponding to the ordinary archimedean absolute value, and one finite place for each prime number $p$, corresponding to the $p$-adic absolute value.
nodes.title: Places of $\mathbb{Q}$

nodes.summary: Let $v$ be a place of $\mathbb{Q}$, let $|\cdot|_v$ be the absolute value attached to $v$, and let $\mathbb{Q}_v$ be the completed field at $v$. The canonical embedding of $\mathbb{Q}$, equipped with the metric $d(x, y) = |x - y|_v$, into $\mathbb{Q}_v$ is an isometry: for all $x, y \in \mathbb{Q}$, the distance between the images of $x$ and $y$ in $\mathbb{Q}_v$ equals $|x - y|_v$.
nodes.title: The embedding of $\mathbb{Q}$ into its completion at a place is an isometry

nodes.summary: For a place $v$ of $\mathbb{Q}$, the ring homomorphism from $\mathbb{Q}$, equipped with the absolute value $|\cdot|_v$ attached to $v$ as its norm, into the completed field $\mathbb{Q}_v$ given by the canonical embedding of $\mathbb{Q}$ ($\mathbb{Q}_v = \mathbb{R}$ at the infinite place and $\mathbb{Q}_v = \mathbb{Q}_p$ at a prime $p$).
nodes.title: Embedding of $\mathbb{Q}$, normed by a place, into its completion

fully_proved.label: fully proved

inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.
